A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPLB-SP and OPSE-LCMDP research. Full text and rendered pages, including all appendices, support comparison; retained algorithms and proofs can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, but no original empirical outcomes. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees rather than experimental measurements.

after.justification: Appendix F and Figure 1 report original simulations in synthetic tabular, media-streaming, and synthetic linear CMDPs, including regret, constraint violations, and safe-policy deployment counts.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same estimation, optimistic-pessimistic updates, safe-policy deployment rules, clipped value functions, composite softmax policy, and bisection search. The new experiments and explanatory clarifications do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 contains no empirical evaluation. v3 adds three evaluated environments: randomly generated tabular CMDPs, media streaming with buffer dynamics and service-use constraints, and synthetic linear CMDPs with more states than feature dimensions.

E2.justification: v3 introduces actual empirical comparisons with Ghosh et al. (2024) and a uniform policy in all three environments. DOPE, attributed to Bura et al. (2022), participates in the tabular and media-streaming comparisons but is explicitly omitted from the synthetic linear experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces evaluation over 10,000 episodes with horizon H=4, specified environment sizes and safety thresholds, and heuristically selected algorithm parameters. It evaluates exact regret, positive-part violation regret, and safe-policy deployment counts. These are new experimental protocols, with no earlier empirical settings to revise.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a focused diagnostic of cumulative safe-policy deployments across training in all three environments. It examines whether reliance on the safe policy subsides, supplementing the theoretical deployment bound. No component ablations or distribution-shift tests are added.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports averaging results over 10 random seeds and displays shaded bands in Figure 1. Their statistical meaning is not specified in the text or caption. v1 has no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds all empirical results: OPSE-LCMDP and Ghosh et al. (2024) exhibit sublinear regret, while only OPSE-LCMDP maintains zero violation across all three environments. DOPE also reports zero violation in its two evaluated environments, and safe-policy deployment counts plateau. These are new findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix C, Theorem 41 becomes v3 Appendix D, Theorem 5, with safe-policy-round regret corrected from B|U| to 2B|U| and the corresponding constant increased from 32 to 64. The safety-type reduction also corrects its indicator to penalize unsafe rather than safe pairs. The main CMDP guarantee and proof framework remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: computationally efficient linear-CMDP exploration with episode-wise safety and square-root regret, enabled by the safe-policy deployment rule and softmax-based optimistic-pessimistic exploration. The experiments provide additional support without broadening these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 Remark 1 expands the discussion of unresolved regret dependence and cautions against comparing bounds under different safety requirements. The conclusion newly explains why adversarial initial states require further analysis, alongside the retained multi-constraint limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds environment-generation procedures, numerical hyperparameters, comparator implementation descriptions, and a source-code location. It also reports execution within 30 minutes using eight Intel Core i7 CPUs and 32 GiB RAM. v1 lacks this empirical implementation and resource information.

R1.justification: Table 1 refocuses the theoretical comparison around Yu et al. (2024), Ghosh et al. (2024), Roknilamouki et al. (2025), and a bandit lower bound. References also add Dann et al. and Lattimore and Szepesvari, while dropping Yang et al. (2022) and Wei et al. (2024). The main research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The bandit-to-CMDP narrative and main section hierarchy are retained. v3 tightens prose, clarifies that mixture policies are proof devices, adds a symbol glossary, and moves existing preliminary definitions into the useful-lemmas appendix. Author affiliations and theorem labeling are also updated.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template with a reorganized author block, changed typography and spacing, shaded theorem boxes, and boxed remarks. Table 1 is substantially restructured, and the new Figure 1 contains nine experimental panels with legends and shaded bands.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful empirical corroboration of the retained theory, corrects specific mathematical errors, and makes implementation and applicability limits easier to assess. The gains are bounded: the central algorithm and asymptotic guarantee remain unchanged, and the small simulations use heuristic tuning and undefined uncertainty bands. Overall, the paper becomes more informative and precise without a substantial change in its foundational contribution.
